statement.excerpt: Before I go any further: if anyone has been taking $2.75-per-hour-per-GPU for any kind of Blackwell GPU, they are losing money.
statement.document_title: I Will Never Respect A Website

our_interpretation: Anyone taking the quoted rate means the rental provider receiving payment.
Losing money means rental revenue fails to cover attributable ownership and operating costs, including capital consumption, rather than merely failing to cover electricity.
The context describes an hourly spot-price comparison covering roughly February through April 2026. Assess that interval rather than importing a provider's unrelated fiscal quarter.
The quoted press estimate concerns rental prices. It does not supply an accounting basis for Zitron's separate loss assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Provider-specific records or a defensible universal cost floor show attributable costs above USD 2.75 per billed GPU-hour for every Blackwell configuration covered by the claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one provider demonstrably covers all relevant costs while receiving USD 2.75 per Blackwell GPU-hour during the target period, on an accounting basis matching the claim.

evidence.locator: B200 (Blackwell): The Future, If You Can Get It
evidence.explanation: The marketplace reports widely varying March reserved rental prices, including rates near the asserted threshold. Asking prices do not reveal provider costs or establish profitability, and reserved terms differ from spot rentals.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: For February 1–April 14, 2026, records showing at least one provider covered all attributable costs at $2.75 per billed Blackwell GPU-hour would contradict the claim. Provider records or a defensible universal cost floor showing costs above that rate for every covered configuration would support it. Costs must include capital recovery, financing, power, hosting and shared costs, with explicit utilization and residual-value assumptions.
